findings.title: ValidationError interpolated into log leaks *arr API response payload values
findings.problem: The change replaces the bounded `exc.error_count()` summary with the full `str(exc)` of a pydantic.ValidationError. Pydantic v2 renders each error with its `input` value inline (e.g. `Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value='...', input_type=...]`), so the raw upstream API response fields are written into the log and into the web UI log buffer. The redacting sink at triggarr/logging.py only does literal `text.replace(secret, ...)` against `collect_secrets` values (configured API keys, password_hash, session_secret) — it cannot mask arbitrary response content. This also contradicts the codebase's own established convention: triggarr/search/engine.py `_sanitize_exc` deliberately maps ValidationError to `f"validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)"` with the docstring "Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink" — which is precisely the formatting this diff removes.
findings.current_code:
except pydantic.ValidationError as exc:
            logger.warning(
                "{app}: Unexpected API response format: {exc}",
                app=self._app_name,
                exc=exc,
            )
            return False
findings.fix_hint: reuse the existing convention: log `_sanitize_exc(exc)` (or restore `exc.error_count()`), and put the verbose `str(exc)` behind logger.debug if the detail is wanted for troubleshooting
findings.why_it_matters: A single malformed *arr response writes unbounded upstream payload content to stderr and to the UI-visible log buffer, where the redacting sink cannot mask it. It also silently diverges from the sanitize-exceptions rule the rest of the codebase documents and follows.

findings.title: Raw exc interpolation bypasses the codebase's _sanitize_exc exception-sanitization pattern
findings.problem: The diff replaces type/status-based exception summaries with raw `exc` interpolation, bypassing the codebase's established exception-sanitization pattern for httpx/pydantic errors. The established solution is `_sanitize_exc(exc)` in triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44, whose docstring states its purpose verbatim: 'Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink.' It handles exactly the two exception classes this diff touches — `httpx.HTTPStatusError` -> `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` (identical to the code the diff DELETED at line 234) and `pydantic.ValidationError` -> `f"validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)"` (identical to the code the diff DELETED at line 253). Established call sites, well past the rule of three: triggarr/search/engine.py:366, :618, :880, :1137 and triggarr/search/scheduler.py:408 (whose comment states 'httpx/pydantic exceptions route through `_sanitize_exc` (engine.py) to strip `request.url` credentials that may contain `apikey=` query parameters'). Two further sites inline the same type-based summary rather than raw exc: triggarr/tracking.py:71-74 and triggarr/clients/base.py:71-75 — the latter is 160 lines above the change, in the SAME FILE, in `_request_with_retry`, so the diff now makes base.py internally inconsistent with itself. Note the redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py:36-42) is a plain `str.replace` over the CONFIGURED secret list, so it does cover the startup path (triggarr/startup.py:198 calls setup_logging before :220 validate_connections) — this is a defense-in-depth/consistency regression, not a confirmed leak, which is why it is scoped to pattern-consistency at medium rather than escalated.

findings.title: _sanitize_exc lives in search/engine.py but is needed by the transport layer (clients/base.py)
findings.problem: Layering/placement observation that the diff surfaces: the shared exception-sanitization helper `_sanitize_exc` lives in triggarr/search/engine.py (a domain/orchestration module) but is needed by the transport layer (triggarr/clients/base.py) and by tracking. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:408 already reaches across for it (its own comment names the source: '`_sanitize_exc` (engine.py)'), and triggarr/tracking.py:71-74 plus triggarr/clients/base.py:71-75 both hand-inline a near-copy of the same logic rather than import it — three sites total sharing one concern with no shared home. Because the helper is underscore-private and sits in the wrong layer, the path of least resistance for a client-layer author is exactly what this diff did: skip it. That is the structural reason the pattern was bypassed. pending: I did not read scheduler.py's import block to confirm the engine->scheduler direction is a one-way import (no cycle claimed); confidence is capped because the layering argument rests on module naming plus the three sites I read, not on a documented layering convention in this repo.

findings.title: pydantic.ValidationError str() echoes raw *arr response payload into web-exposed log buffer
findings.problem: The diff replaces `count=exc.error_count()` with `exc=exc`, so the full `str(ValidationError)` is now interpolated into the log message. Pydantic v2 renders `input_value=...` for every failing field — i.e. the raw upstream JSON fragment that failed validation. I reproduced this locally: validating `{'version': {'apiKey': 'SECRET123'}}` renders `Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value={'apiKey': 'SECRET123'}, input_type=dict]`. This message reaches two sinks: the stderr redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py:36) AND `buffer_sink` (triggarr/logging.py:72), which feeds `log_buffer` rendered in the web UI at triggarr/web/routes.py:389 and :1199. Redaction is exact-substring only over the secrets list from `collect_secrets` (triggarr/startup.py:87-99) — it catches the configured API key verbatim, but any OTHER field in a malformed *arr response (session tokens, internal paths, user data echoed by a reverse proxy or an error page) passes through unredacted. This also directly contradicts the codebase's own stated convention: `_sanitize_exc` at triggarr/search/engine.py:29-43 exists precisely to avoid `str(exc)` because it "may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink", and it handles `pydantic.ValidationError` with exactly the `error_count()` form this diff removes. The diff moves base.py away from the pattern engine.py was written to enforce.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
    "{app}: Unexpected API response format: {exc}",
    app=self._app_name,
    exc=exc,
)
findings.fix_hint: Reuse the existing convention: log `_sanitize_exc(exc)` (or restore `exc.error_count()`) instead of the raw exception, and put the full detail behind `logger.debug` if the verbosity is the actual goal.
findings.why_it_matters: Validation failures are exactly the case where the response body is unexpected and therefore unvetted — that arbitrary payload is now written verbatim into a log buffer surfaced in the web UI, where the redaction guarantee only covers values already known to `collect_secrets`.

findings.title: HTTPStatusError str() puts the full instance URL (including any query credentials) in the log line
findings.problem: `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` renders as `Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url 'http://radarr.local:7878/api/v3/system/status?...'` — verified by reproduction. Previously only `exc.response.status_code` was logged. The base URL is user-configured, so this now writes the operator's internal *arr host/port into both stderr and the web-visible `log_buffer`. Triggarr sends its key via the `X-Api-Key` header (base.py:32), not the query string, so the configured key is not normally in the URL — and if it were, the exact-substring redacting sink would catch it. The residual exposure is therefore the internal URL and any non-secret query parameters, not the API key itself, which is why this is scoped low rather than high. Note the same file's own retry handler at base.py:66-76 deliberately narrows to `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` for this exact reason; this diff makes the two handlers in one file disagree about the rule. pending: confirm whether exposing the internal *arr URL in the UI log viewer is acceptable to the maintainer — it may be considered benign for a self-hosted single-operator tool.

findings.title: Raw HTTP exceptions leak reverse-proxy credentials
findings.problem: A configured URL containing basic-auth credentials is accepted. On a non-401 HTTP failure, httpx includes that full URL in the exception text. Reproduced with a 502: the message contains `http://proxyuser:proxy-password@localhost:7878/api/v3/system/status`. collect_secrets() excludes URL credentials, so both stderr and the web log buffer retain the password.
findings.why_it_matters: A basic-auth password embedded in the configured instance URL is written to stderr and the web log buffer on any non-401 HTTP failure; collect_secrets() does not cover URL credentials, so the redacting sink cannot mask it.
findings.fix_hint: Keep logging the status code, or explicitly sanitize the URL before logging structured error details. Add a regression test asserting URL credentials never reach either logging sink on a 502.
